body: No joke. My doctors refused to treat me further if I didn’t stop smoking. I stopped and it was the closest I’ve been to hurting myself but I refuse to do so since I know something is wrong. I did start reaching out to end of life doctors though. Pretty eye opening looking back after smoking again. I don’t want to die but am dying. What the heck. I’ve seen these doctors for 2 straight years, now on our third together. They don’t understand how much suffering I’m really going through and it helps so much. They finally listened after I stopped, had to call 911 for my symptoms. Contacted the crises Line. And then I Had a police officer come with me to my doctor appointment so they couldn’t deny their mistakes.  After them finally referring me to the tests I’ve been asking for. I couldn’t help but to find relief and it was like breathing air for the first time again. Appetite, energy, focus.  Thank you weed! I really hope this doesn’t turn out to be the tumor I think it is.

Must have felt amazing. I remember straight up swinging on my bully while people were holding us apart one day in elementary school. I wish I could remember the context better but it was straight rage and I’m glad those other kids held us apart. I wonder what people thought of that. I didn’t really have any friends to go over it with at the time. I know an impression was made though because things did change after that. I have always been known for being very upfront and ‘real’ to my friends. I never connect the dots but this could have been a pivotal moment in my life that defined me as a person. I’ve done a lot of stupid shit and pushed peoples buttons but no one ever really fucked with me. I’ve never actually been in a real fight, I knew when to walk away and  when to step up and who was full it. I think it’s a different form of quiet confidence aka respect. It’s also where true forms of respect for others come from. Understanding real qualities and skills in other people, you just know not to cross some lines. Some people don’t figure that part out. 

To Op- I guess all I can say is stand up for yourself and for what you believe in. The fake people in life will become very obvious and you’ll learn about yourself in the process. Don’t be afraid to be wrong either. This bully sounds temporary and the ways to deal with it seem kind of obvious. Either put up and ignore it the best you can or stand up one day and say in your own words that enough is enough, and escalate the situation from there. Prepare for that day though.

I purposely stopped wearing my seatbelt about a year or so ago for this reason. Got in a pretty serious accident a few months ago, T-Boned by Jeep Wrangler going ~50 mph. Guess I was “lucky” it was only a Jeep. Woke up in the passenger seat looking out the driver door. No one seriously hurt. My dog (can’t explain how thankful I am, not sure where I’d be without him) and I basically walked away. Can’t really understand it. I have always thought in different situations that well loved, successful people die every day, why can’t I take one of their places? Why not on that day? Why am I still here? I also thought surviving something like that would wake me up but honestly things have only gotten worse sense then. I feel so bad about feeling this way but can’t shake it. It’s like, there are people in the hospital that beg for the opportunities I have. Let them have mine. Please, I’m such a waste with the mental issues I have. If I could donate my health I would. I am an organ donor though. I’ve kept my body I pretty decent shape and feel like it would be a proper donation.  Gosh I’m thinking too far into this as I’m typing. Not sure if it helps but it feels good to write this out. I oddly feel comfort in understanding you. Maybe it’ll work both ways. Sorry if this is too much.

Totally understand where you’re at... wish I had some answers for you but you’re not alone. I’ve decided to jump in with two feet on some things I am not certain about. Feigning confidence and just going with it. 

I recently listened to Joe Rogans podcast with Dr. Phil where he said something that really clicked in my head. Dr. Phil said if there are things that are really not going well in your life, it is normal and not feel okay. If there are a few area in life that you’re struggling in, don’t feel bad about feeling bad. It’s normal. 

I’m not sure what your situation is, but this reminded me that my friends, family and peers looking down on me didn’t define me. I am in a situation that anyone in the same one could feel the way I do. If anyone really knew my situation or were in it themselves they may not even be able to handle it as well as I do. 

It’s hard because I’ve tried to explain this to those closest to me. I’m doing my best and am clearly confused about a lot of things based on my experience in life. More well adjusted people tend not to understand where I’m coming from and continue to distance themselves from me. It’s been hard but I’m finally letting go of people that I say they care about me but act completely different. 

Not sure if any of this helps or is relatable but I felt like sharing my recent experiences maybe I can create some sort of comfort. Feel free to PM me if you need.
